items.title: Bernstein's 2027 Bitcoin Price Target
points: Bernstein released a new Bitcoin price target for 2027, signaling analyst expectations for cryptocurrency valuations over the coming year.
CoinMarketCap published latest industry news and data updates on crypto market developments.

items.title: Ethereum's Speed Roadmap: Four Parallel Workstreams
points: Roadmap targets four speed improvements: fast blocks, fast finality, a fast confirmation rule, and fast interoperability.
Fast blocks: removes the fixed 12-second block time, cutting it to 10 seconds in the upcoming Hegotá fork—possibly the last practical window for years to reduce block times.

Fast finality: an Ethereum Foundation/Consensys proposal to compress finality (the point at which a transaction is permanently confirmed and can't be reversed) from about 15 minutes down to a couple of minutes in a later fork.
Fast Confirmation Rule: a near-production protocol, already adopted by one major bridge, that cuts confirmation to tens of seconds with formally provable security guarantees.

Fast interoperability: real-time zero-knowledge proving (cryptographic verification that enables instant asset transfers between blockchain layers without revealing transaction details) to speed up Layer 2-to-Layer 1 asset flows.

items.title: Bitwise Automated Token Portfolios & On-Chain Self-Custody
points: Bitwise launched Automated Token Portfolios on Coinbase's tokenized stocks (NVDAc, METAc, AAPLc, GOOGLc) deployed on the Base blockchain, live two days before launch.
Lets non-US investors hold institution-grade equity exposure in self-custody wallets (personal crypto wallets where users retain full control of assets) with automated rebalancing.
Non-custodial structure: Bitwise sets target allocations, users hold tokens in personal wallets, and Glider's automated protocol maintains balance without taking control of assets.
Restricted to non-US persons under Regulation S, targeting eligible international jurisdictions.

items.title: South Korea's Stablecoin Financial Infrastructure Play
points: Shinhan Financial Group partnered with Visa to build stablecoin-based (crypto tokens pegged to a stable asset like a currency) financial infrastructure for payments, settlements, and remittances.
Piloting won-denominated (Korean currency) tokenized funds with Solana ecosystem partners.
Pilot programs will test stablecoins in card payment settlement, AI-based payment models, and B2B/B2C payments across Shinhan Bank, Shinhan Card, and Jeju Bank.
Follows an April Shinhan Card partnership with Solana Foundation and an August MOU with Solana, Etherfuse, and Orca, as South Korea develops its Digital Asset Basic Act.

items.title: Market Snapshot: Bitcoin, XRP, and Altcoins
points: Bitcoin held near $79,000 as traders banked a 23% weekly gain.
XRP rallied 45% over the week.
Altcoins like Ether and Solana retreated 4% amid short-term profit-taking.

items.title: Grayscale Launches World's First Zcash ETF
points: Grayscale launched the ZCSH ETF, giving traditional brokerage accounts direct access to ZEC (Zcash cryptocurrency).
ZEC features Bitcoin-equivalent tokenomics: a 21 million coin supply cap and a halving schedule (periodic reduction in new coin issuance), plus optional privacy features.

items.title: x402 Micropayment Fee Economics Challenge
points: x402 (a micropayment protocol) hit 1–1.5 million transactions daily for the first time, with volume up 2x versus June/July.
Average transaction size collapsed to $0.023–$0.031 (less than 3 cents).
Popular third-party facilitators charge a flat $0.001 per settlement, so fees now consume 32–43% of average transaction value, making economics unworkable for merchants.

Batching (settling thousands of transactions in one on-chain proof) could cut costs 90–99% and has been available since May, but adoption remains near zero due to unclear blockers around tooling, counterparty risk, or accounting complexity.
